questions.question: A life annuity has annual payment rate 1200 and pays monthly while the annuitant survives. What amount is paid at each monthly date?
A unit-rate life annuity pays $1/m$ each $1/m$ year while alive, with integer $m\ge 1$. Which pair of first-payment formulas for the due and immediate versions is valid for every such $m$?
An $m$-times-yearly unit-rate annuity-due has integer payment index $j\ge 0$, integer $m\ge 1$ and annual discount factor $v>0$. Which discount-factor formula is valid for every admitted $j,m,v$?

A half-yearly life annuity-due pays one unit at times 0, 0.5, 1, and so on only while the annuitant is alive. The annuitant dies exactly at time 0.5, and the contract requires $T>s$ for a payment at date $s$, where $T$ is death time. Which receipts occur?

An $m$-times-yearly unit-rate life annuity-due has APV $m^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}v^{j/m}P(T>j/m)$, with future lifetime $T>0$, annual discount factor $v>0$ and finite sum. What does the case $m=1$ represent?
options: The ordinary annual unit life annuity-due.
A single unit payment at issue.
A lifetime unit-rate continuous payment stream.

questions.question: A quarterly life annuity-due pays $1/4$ at dates 0, 0.25, 0.5, and so on while alive. Interest is zero, and the annuitant dies at time 0.7 year. What total amount has been received?

A whole-life annuity pays at annual rate 600 in monthly instalments. Its due and immediate versions use identical later payment dates and survival conditions, and their APVs are finite. How much larger is due APV than immediate APV?
A temporary unit-rate annuity-due pays quarterly for a term of three years, at grid dates before maturity while alive. There are four instalments per year. What is its final possible payment date?
A half-yearly annuity pays at annual rate 200. Its annual discount factor is $v=0.81$, and survival probability to the date 1.5 years is 0.7. What is the APV contribution of that instalment alone?

A unit-rate temporary annuity-due pays half-yearly during the first year, at dates 0 and 0.5. Annual survival is $p=0.8$ and annual discount factor $v=0.81$. Under UDD, survival at fractional duration $s\in[0,1]$ is $1-s(1-p)$. What is the APV?

A one-year unit-rate annuity-due pays half-yearly at dates 0 and 0.5. Annual survival probability is $p$ with $0<p<1$ and annual discount factor is $v>0$. UDD gives half-year survival $(1+p)/2$, while CFM gives $\sqrt p$. How do the two APVs compare?
options: The UDD APV is strictly larger.
The APVs agree because annual survival agrees.
The CFM APV is strictly larger.
The comparison depends on whether $v$ is above or below 1.

questions.question: A life annuity pays half-yearly, with annual effective interest rate $i=0.21$ and annual discount factor $v=(1+i)^{-1}$. Which discount factor applies over half a year?

Let $S(t)=P(T>t)$ for $T>0$ and let $0<v\le 1$. All unit-rate due annuity APVs are finite. Refine frequency $m$ to $rm$, with integers $m\ge 1,r\ge 2$. Which comparison holds for every such survivor function and all admissible $v,m,r$?
options: The $rm$-frequency APV is no smaller than the $m$-frequency APV.
The two APVs must agree because their annual payment rates agree.
The refined APV is exactly $1/r$ of the original APV.
The $rm$-frequency APV is no greater than the $m$-frequency APV.

questions.question: An annuitant has annual survival probability $p=0.81$ in every year, with CFM within each year. Annual discount factor is $v=0.81$. A unit-rate whole-life annuity-due pays half-yearly. What is its APV?

A two-year temporary unit-rate annuity-due pays at times 0, 0.5, 1 and 1.5. Annual discount factor is $v=0.81$. Annual survival is 0.81 in the first year and 0.64 in the second, with CFM separately within each year. What is its APV?

A one-year unit-rate half-yearly annuity-due pays at dates 0 and 0.5; its temporary immediate counterpart pays at 0.5 and 1. They use the same survival model, with survival probability 0.64 at year 1 and annual discount factor 0.81. What is due APV minus immediate APV?

Interest is zero and future lifetime is uniform on $(0.35,0.45)$ years. Compare unit-rate whole-life annuities-due paying twice or three times per year while alive. Does moving from two to three payments per year necessarily reduce realised PV?
options: Yes: splitting annual payments more finely always lowers a due value.
No: here the PV rises from $1/2$ to $2/3$.
No: here both realised PVs equal the exact lifetime.
Yes: here the PV falls from $1/2$ to $1/3$.

questions.question: Future lifetime has survival $S(t)=\mathrm{e}^{-0.1t}$ for $t\ge0$ years. The annual discount factor is $v=\mathrm{e}^{0.1}$, so interest is negative. Unit-rate due and immediate annuities pay $1/m$ at their surviving grid dates, for fixed integer $m\ge1$. Which conclusion about APVs and their numerical difference is justified?
options: Both APVs are finite, and their difference is $1/m$.
The due APV is infinite, but removing the issue payment makes the immediate APV finite.
Both APVs are infinite, but subtracting them gives $1/m$.
Both APVs are infinite, so their numerical difference is undefined.

questions.question: Interest is zero and annual survival probability is $p=0.64$ at every integer age. Model U uses UDD within each year; model C uses CFM. Both have annual annuity-due APV $1/(1-p)=25/9$. For unit-rate half-yearly due payments, what do their APVs show?
options: Model U gives $91/36\approx2.52778$; model C gives $2.5$, so annual APV alone is insufficient.
Both give $25/9$, because the annual table and annual benefit rates agree.
Both give $25/18$, because each instalment is half an annual unit.
Model U gives $2.5$; model C gives $91/36$, so annual APV alone is insufficient.

questions.question: Future lifetime has constant mortality force $\lambda=0.2$ per year, so survival is $\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda t}$. Discounting at time $t$ is $\mathrm{e}^{-\delta t}$ with interest force $\delta=0.3$ per year. A unit-rate whole-life annuity-due pays $1/m$ each $1/m$ year while alive. What is the limit of its APV as integer $m$ tends to infinity?
options: $0$ because every instalment amount tends to zero.
